title: The Paper Boat Race
moral: Winning is nice, but helping others along the way is better. True success is not selfish.

pages.text:
After the rain stopped, the lane outside Yusuf's house had small streams of water running beside the footpath.

Yusuf and his friends made paper boats from old notebook pages.

"My boat is the fastest," said Rehan.

"It has not even moved," said Sana.

"It is thinking," Rehan replied.

Everyone laughed.

Yusuf made a neat white boat and wrote his name on it. He folded the edges carefully. He wanted to win the race to the drain cover.

The children placed their boats in the water.

"One, two, three!" shouted Sana.

The boats began to float.

Yusuf's boat moved fast at first. Then it slowed near a pile of leaves.

Rehan's boat passed it.

Yusuf reached down and moved a leaf away. His boat started again.

Then he saw Sana's boat stuck near a stone.

"Help!" Sana said. "My boat is parked."

Yusuf looked ahead. Rehan's boat was still moving. If Yusuf stopped to help, he might lose.

Sana tried to reach, but her hand was too short.

Yusuf sighed and bent down. He moved the stone gently. Sana's boat floated free.

"Thank you!" she said.

Now Yusuf's boat was behind.

He ran beside the stream, cheering for it.

"Come on, slow champion!"

Near the end, Rehan's boat turned sideways and got stuck in a twig. Yusuf's boat floated past it and reached the drain cover first.

"I won!" Yusuf shouted.

Then he looked back.

Sana's boat came second. Rehan's boat was still trapped.

Rehan made a sad face. "My boat retired early."

Yusuf walked back and freed it.

The boat floated slowly to the finish.

All three clapped.

Sana said, "Now every boat finished."

Yusuf looked at his wet fingers and muddy sandals.

Winning had felt good. But helping everyone finish felt better.

Later, when the paper boats became soft and wrinkled, Yusuf placed his boat on the wall to dry.

The ink of his name had spread a little. But beside it, Sana had written one word: Helper.

Yusuf smiled. That word felt better than first place.
